add_grocery_item.name: add_grocery_item
add_grocery_item.description: Add an item to the grocery list by label. Works for any product: food ingredients, household supplies, hygiene items, etc. If a matching product exists, its preferred store is auto-assigned. For unknown products, determine the store from store descriptions (e.g. potatoes → greengrocer, toilet paper → supermarket). Set storeId directly when you can determine it. Only ask the user when you genuinely cannot determine the right store. A product appears once on the list: adding one already there (not yet ticked) accumulates on its line, next to the needs of the planned meals, instead of making a second line — even in another unit (« 300 g + 2 pièces » stays one line). A product bought in a packaging (pack, jar…) is always counted in packagings, whatever the unit given: « Riz » alone is one pack, « Riz 300 g » of a 500 g pack is one pack too (rounded up to whole packagings).

assign_product_store.name: assign_product_store
assign_product_store.description: Set the preferred/fallback store, the shelf life and the aisle of a product. shelfLifeDays indicates how many days the product stays fresh (null = non-perishable). aisle puts the product in an aisle of a store, by aisle id or by name — a name the store does not have yet creates the aisle, last on the way through the store (see manage_aisles); an empty string leaves the product without an aisle there. The aisle is in aisleStoreId, else in the preferred store (the one given here, or the product's). A product has one aisle per store: « Crèmerie » at one store and « Frais » at another are two calls.

cancel_proaction.name: cancel_proaction
cancel_proaction.description: Cancel a proaction by its id (from list_proactions): it is removed from the « Maggie » agenda and will not run. This time only — to stop a lasting habit, change the instruction instead.

check_conflicts.name: check_conflicts
check_conflicts.description: Check for scheduling conflicts at a given date, time, and duration. Date format: YYYY-MM-DD. Time format: HH:MM. Duration in minutes (default 60).

check_grocery_item.name: check_grocery_item
check_grocery_item.description: Toggle the checked state of a grocery item. Set checked=true when bought, false to uncheck.

check_routine.name: check_routine
check_routine.description: Tick a routine as done on a day, or take the tick back. id is the routine's (list_routines gives it — call it with the date first when the user names the routine by its title). date is YYYY-MM-DD, today (the user's timezone) when left out; a day to come, or before the routine existed, is refused. done=false removes the tick. Ticking twice or removing a tick that is not there changes nothing. A routine may be ticked on a day it was not due. Returns {success, date, checked, routine} as list_routines reads the routine. Say it is noted, nothing more: no congratulations, no streak.

claim_due_proactions.name: claim_due_proactions
claim_due_proactions.description: Reserved for the proaction executor — never call it in a conversation. Claims the pending proactions whose time has come and marks them running, atomically: a proaction is claimed once, however many executors ask. Each comes with its userId and prompt; report the outcome with record_proaction_result. With id, claims that one pending proaction now, whether its time has come or not (the manual trigger); an empty list when it is not pending.

create_event.name: create_event

reminders.description: minutes before the start, e.g. [60] for "une heure avant"

create_event.description: Create a new calendar event. Always give the whole schedule — a start and an end, never a duration, nothing is assumed: start_date (YYYY-MM-DD) + start_time (HH:MM) + end_date + end_time, or for a whole-day event all_day true + start_date + end_date, where end_date is EXCLUDED — the day after the last day, as in Google Calendar's API: the 1st of January alone is start_date 2037-01-01 and end_date 2037-01-02, « du 26 au 28 janvier » is start_date the 26th and end_date the 29th. For "du X au Y", holidays, a trip or any stretch of several days, make ONE whole-day event with all_day true, start_date and end_date: never simulate a range with rrule (that makes one event per day) or with a long timed event. An event running past midnight has an end_date the day after. An incomplete schedule, or an end that is not after the start, creates nothing and returns an error. The result gives the schedule that was saved, in the event's own time zone (event.allDay; event.startAt and event.endAt for a timed event; for a whole-day event, whose startAt and endAt are null, event.startDate, event.endDate excluded and event.lastDay — tell the user the days it covers, « le 1er janvier » or « du 26 au 28 », from startDate to lastDay, never « jusqu'au » the excluded end): announce exactly that to the user, not what you meant to do. The result also gives the day of the week of what was saved (event.weekday, and startWeekday, endWeekday or lastDayWeekday next to each date): check that it is the day you announced to the user — « lundi 26 » must come back lundi — and if it is not, fix the event before confirming. Never work out a day of the week yourself: take it from these fields, from the weekday of a read tool, or from the date_time tool. Pass agenda_id whenever the user said or implied where the event belongs — its name as they said it ("Concerts", "au boulot": case, accents and approximations do not matter) or its id, with no manage_agendas call first. Omit it when they said nothing about the agenda: the tool then works it out from the event itself, from the agendas' names and descriptions, and from the agenda the user filed similar events in before. Two agendas fitting equally well, or a name matching none, returns an error naming the plausible agendas and creates nothing — ask the user which one they mean and retry, never pick one yourself. Tell the user which agenda the event went to: it is in event.agenda. Use reminders for "préviens-moi une heure avant": a list of delays in minutes before the start, e.g. [60] or [10, 1440]; omit it when the user asked for nothing. Use rrule for a repeating event, RFC 5545 without the RRULE: prefix — "FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO", "FREQ=DAILY;COUNT=10", "FREQ=MONTHLY;INTERVAL=2". The start given is the first occurrence, and reminders then fire for every occurrence. Use status 'tentative' when the user says "provisoire", "à confirmer", "peut-être" or "sous réserve"; omit it (or 'confirmed') for an ordinary event. Say so in your answer when the event is tentative (event.status).

create_recipe.name: create_recipe
create_recipe.description: Create a new recipe. Ingredients is a JSON array of objects with quantity, unit, and either ingredientId or ciqualAlimCode (to auto-create an Ingredient from Ciqual). Tags is a comma-separated list. Utensils is a JSON array of what the recipe is made with, each a utensil id (from manage_utensils) or a name — a name not in the catalogue yet is added to it. The method goes in steps, notes keep the tips. Steps is a JSON array of the steps, in order (the first is step 1), each {text, durationMinutes?, background?, ingredientIds?, utensils?, waitsFor?}: ingredientIds names ingredients of the recipe by ingredientId or by name (only a link: a partial quantity goes in the text); utensils are utensil ids or names, added to the recipe's utensils; background (needs a duration) means the timer runs while the cook moves on; waitsFor lists the positions of earlier steps that must be finished first.

create_task.name: create_task
create_task.description: Create a new task. Priority: low/medium/high. Criticality: low/medium/high/critical. Due date format: YYYY-MM-DD. To make it a subtask, give parentId — the id of a task that is not a subtask itself (one level only). estimatedMinutes (1 to 1440) is how long it should take, firstStep the first small gesture that starts it; both stay in Maggie, Google never sees them.

delete_event.name: delete_event
delete_event.description: Delete a calendar event by its ID. Returns confirmation of deletion. When the user names the event rather than gives its id (« supprime le piano du jeudi »), find it first with get_upcoming_events and query (the distinctive word(s) of its title, no days: it searches the next year), or search with types events — never from a 7-day window, and never answer that it is not found before that search came back empty. A recurring series is designated by its master event: the id the search returns is the series' own, and deleting it removes every occurrence.

delete_recipe.name: delete_recipe
delete_recipe.description: Delete a recipe by ID. Meals that have no other recipe are deleted with it (their shopping leaves the grocery list); meals with other recipes keep them. Returns deletedMeals, the number of meals deleted.

delete_task.name: delete_task
delete_task.description: Delete a task by its ID. Returns confirmation of deletion.

detect_internal_transfers.name: detect_internal_transfers
detect_internal_transfers.description: Pair the movements that went from one of the user's accounts to another, over his history. A transfer between two of his own accounts is neither an expense nor an income, so both legs leave every figure: the lifestyle measured, the saving capacity, the monthly review and the day-over-year comparison of the score. Two lines pair when they are on two different accounts of his, carry exactly opposite amounts in the same currency, are booked four days apart at most, and are already spent or committed. limitDays narrows the pass to the last days (the whole history by default), dryRun reports the pairs it would write without writing any of them — use it first and tell the user which lines would be paired. A transfer from a savings or investment account to a checking one booked while the salary was late is marked advance instead (each pair says its transferKind, advances counts them; get_savings_advances says what is left to give back). A transfer from the checking account to that source whose amount equals exactly what is left of an open advance is marked repayment and settles it (repayments counts them; a partial amount stays an internal transfer). A line whose other leg is not there (an account that is not synced) is still marked internal, with no counterpart, when its label or counterparty names the holder (his name, in any case or order) or, on a transfer, the bank of another of his accounts (loneLegs lists them with the reason, holder or bank; it pairs later if the other leg arrives, and a recurring operation never takes it). A line he marked by hand is never requalified. To mark or unmark one line, use manage_transactions with action update, transferKind and counterpartId.

end_errand.name: end_errand
end_errand.description: End shopping errand. Archives all checked (bought) items as past errands, one per store (errands: id, storeName, itemCount; read them back with list_past_errands), and removes them from the list, puts the products they carried back In Stock (restockedProducts: tell the user which ones) and returns remaining unchecked items. The agent should then ask the user about EACH remaining item: keep on the list for later, or remove. Use remove_grocery_item to remove items the user no longer wants.

envelope_adjustments.name: envelope_adjustments
envelope_adjustments.description: Adjust the monthly envelopes to what was really spent ("mes enveloppes sont-elles adaptées ?"). month is YYYY-MM, the month read (defaults to the current one); the amounts proposed are for the month after it. The suggest action lists every monthly envelope of the month with its amountCents, what was really spent (actualCents), what the next month is budgeted at (targetAmountCents) and — only for the envelopes that do not fit — a suggestion {proposedCents, direction raise or lower, reason, seasonal}. An envelope fits, and has no suggestion, unless it was exceeded three months running with spending mostly judged worth keeping (raise), was left under three quarters of its amount three months running (lower), or the same month of the past years was far from next month's amount (a season: seasonal {fromMonth, toMonth} names the month, and the amount is for that month of every year). Spending mostly judged avoidable never raises an envelope. Give the reason as it is, in French, it says why. Nothing is written by suggest. The apply action writes next month's amounts for the suggestions of categoryIds (comma-separated category ids; all of them when omitted) — only after the owner agreed: never apply on your own. Amounts are integer cents, divide by 100 to speak them.

generate_grocery_list.name: generate_grocery_list
generate_grocery_list.description: Top up the grocery list with the recurring items that are due again; running it twice changes nothing. Meals add nothing by themselves: mealsToChoose names the meals of the date range whose ingredients the owner has not chosen yet (id, date, slot, summary) — offer to choose them with manage_meal_groceries (preview, then add). Date format: YYYY-MM-DD.

get_day_plan.name: get_day_plan
get_day_plan.description: Read the user's day: at most 5 slots, each a task to do that day, in order. date is YYYY-MM-DD, today (the user's timezone) when left out; an empty day is created on first read. Returns slots [{position, type, task}], now (the first slot not done: what to do now, or null), reserve (every other open task that is not a subtask, highest orderScore first — the tasks waiting, not shown on the day), done and total (the ring: done slots out of the slots), confirmedAt (null while the day is only proposed). Each task has id, title, estimatedMinutes, firstStep, completedAt, dueDate, postponedSince (the day it was put off since — say « reportée », never a reproach), urgency and criticality.

get_event.name: get_event
get_event.description: Get one calendar event by its ID: summary, start, end, all-day flag and agenda. Works for past events too. A whole-day event (allDay true) has no startAt/endAt but startDate, endDate EXCLUDED as in Google's API (the day after its last day) and lastDay: tell the user « le 1er janvier » or « du 26 au 28 » from startDate to lastDay, never « jusqu'au » endDate. Every local date comes with its day of the week (startWeekday, endWeekday for a timed event; startWeekday and lastDayWeekday for a whole-day one): say the weekday from those fields or from the date_time tool (weekday action), never work it out yourself.

get_events_by_date.name: get_events_by_date

agendas.description: names or ids of the agendas to read

get_events_by_date.description: Get all events for a specific date (YYYY-MM-DD format). Returns events from all of the user agendas, including expanded recurring events. A whole-day event (allDay true) has no startAt/endAt but startDate, endDate EXCLUDED as in Google's API (the day after its last day) and lastDay: tell the user « le 1er janvier » or « du 26 au 28 » from startDate to lastDay, never « jusqu'au » endDate. Every local date comes with its day of the week (startWeekday, endWeekday for a timed event; startWeekday and lastDayWeekday for a whole-day one): say the weekday from those fields or from the date_time tool (weekday action), never work it out yourself. Pass agendas (a list of agenda names as the user says them — case, accents and approximations do not matter — or ids) whenever the user asked to be told only about some agendas (« ne me parle que de Défaut et Garde Ael », a rule to apply to every read from then on): only their events come back, and a name matching no agenda returns an error listing the user's agendas and no events at all. Omit it to read every agenda. Each event carries the name of its agenda (agenda) and its times in its own time zone (timeZone): announce those. To find an event by its name on that day, pass query, the distinctive word(s) of its title. When the day is not known, use get_upcoming_events with query instead, never guess a date.

get_finance_dashboard.name: get_finance_dashboard
get_finance_dashboard.description: Read the whole financial picture for a month (defaults to the current one) in one call: `scores` (the week and the month with the amount left to spend, the spending rhythm and the reasons of each status), `tiles` (`accounts`: total, safety cushion and available with every account; `budget`: the root envelopes with consumed against budgeted, the safety cushion, the expected salary and the balance expected the eve of the salary, both null when unknown; `planning`: the independence counter and the net saving capacity; each account of `accounts` carries `rejectionsToSettleCount`), `todo` (what waits for the owner: `toSortCount` lines to sort, `rejectionsToSettleCount` rejected payments not settled, `reviewReady` true while the review of the month just ended is not done, `advanceToRepayCents` still to give back to the savings, `owedToMeCents` what people still owe the owner and `iOweCents` what the owner still owes them — créances and dettes), then the older blocks: `score` (the monthly score with its reasons and the reference salary), the balance of every account, twelve rolling months of money in and out, the budget gauges per envelope, and the five biggest spending posts against the same posts last month. Prefer this over calling the budget, score and loan tools one by one. All amounts are integer cents.

get_finance_scores.name: get_finance_scores
get_finance_scores.description: Read where the user stands in their budget: the score of the week, the score of the month and the global one (the most degraded of the month and the year), for a date (YYYY-MM-DD, defaults to today). Each score is green ("Dans le vert"), neutral ("Dans les clous"), orange ("Attention") or red ("Dépassement"), always with its reasons. Red means the budget of the period is exceeded (for the month also a mandatory category, for the global an annual envelope); otherwise the colour follows the spending rhythm: expected spending at a date is the debits already due (rent, energy, subscriptions: recurring operations) plus the variable part of the budget spread over the days; 95 % of it or more is orange, under 80 % is green. Each week and month carries its rhythm: budgetCents, spentCents, expectedSpentCents, remainingCents, expectedRemainingCents, status (on_track "Dans le rythme" or above "Au-dessus du rythme"), the day-by-day curve and the debits with their dates. Reasons come as codes with amounts in cents (above_rhythm, below_rhythm, on_rhythm, week_budget_exceeded, mandatory_category_exceeded, optional_category_exceeded, plans_exceed_category_budget, total_budget_exceeded, annual_category_exceeded, plans_exceed_annual_category_budget, cushion_incomplete, below_last_year, above_last_year, spending_above_reference_salary, no_budget) — phrase them for the user rather than reading them out.

get_grocery_list.name: get_grocery_list
get_grocery_list.description: Get the grocery list with items grouped by store in visit order, and within a store aisle by aisle in the order of the way through it (`aisle`: {id, name, position}, null for an item without an aisle in that store — those come last), then by position. By default hides deferred items (buyAfter in the future) from the store groups and lists them, with their date, in `later`. Set includeDeferred=true to see them in the store groups instead. A product has one line: the needs of every planned meal, of the restock and of manual additions add up on it. `needed` is that total need in base units (g, ml or the counted unit — « 800 g », or « 300 g + 2 pièces » when the units cannot be added); `quantity` and `unit` are what to buy: for a product bought in a packaging a whole number of packagings counted once on the total (800 g of pasta in 500 g packs is 2 paquets, shown with « 800 g pour les repas »); a product without packaging has no quantity to adjust, its quantity is the need itself. `packaging` (what the product is bought in, with its content when known, e.g. a 500 g pack; null when it has none) and `stockState` (in_stock, low or out).

get_independence_counter.name: get_independence_counter
get_independence_counter.description: Read how far the rentes already cover the way the user lives. Both sides are measured over the last three complete months, never declared: passiveIncomeCents is the monthly average of the credits of the categories flagged as rentes (manage_categories, passiveIncome), lifestyleCents is what a month actually costs, loan payments and exceptional movements excluded. coveragePercent is the first over the second and is NOT capped — above 100 the rentes cover more than the month costs. gapCents is what is still missing each month, byCategory breaks the rentes down, and milestones gives 25/50/75/100 % with the monthly rente each one takes. isMeasurable is false when no month has been measured yet, so there is no percentage to give; hasPassiveIncomeCategories is false when the user has not declared any rente category yet — say that, rather than reporting 0 %. coverageWithDebtPercent is the same ratio against the month including loan payments. projectedCoveragePercent and projectedPassiveIncomeCents are a distinct projection, never to be confused with the measured coveragePercent: the same ratio once the rentes the confirmed recurring series still expect (credits of the rente categories, over the current and next two months, no line attached yet) are added to what already landed; give both and say which is which. The target date of independence and the progression curve are NOT available: they are Premium, so never estimate a date.

get_month_balance.name: get_month_balance
get_month_balance.description: Read the balance of a month (YYYY-MM, defaults to the current one): `spending` (the month status with its budget, what was spent, the expected rhythm and the daily curve), `envelopes` (each root envelope with consumed against budgeted and its status held, close or over), `satisfaction` (what was judged worth keeping against avoidable, and the kept share in percent, null while nothing is judged), `savings` (what was put aside against the planned saving capacity, null when no income is known), `cushion`, and `toQualify` (the count and weight of the lines of the month nobody qualified yet — they belong to no envelope). All amounts are integer cents.

get_purchase_suggestions.name: get_purchase_suggestions
get_purchase_suggestions.description: Products the user buys often and that are due again (« tu en prends souvent »), computed from the past errands: each product bought at least 3 times, with everyDays (median gap between purchases, in days), lastBoughtOn and dueOn (YYYY-MM-DD), usualQuantity and usualUnit (median quantity, null when unknown). Use it for « il me manque quelque chose ? ». Products already on the grocery list, on a recurring grocery item, or dismissed (« Pas besoin ») are left out. To add one, call add_grocery_item with its name and usual quantity.

get_recipe.name: get_recipe
get_recipe.description: Get a recipe by ID with its ingredients, the utensils it is made with and its steps (in order: text, durationMinutes, background, ingredients, utensils, waitsFor — the positions of the steps it waits for). guests (1 or more) answers the quantities scaled to that many people — × guests / servings, rounded as a cook reads them — without changing the recipe; the answer then says scaledFor and scaleFactor.

get_recurring_operations.name: get_recurring_operations
get_recurring_operations.description: Read what the recurring operations (subscriptions, rent, salary, any series the user expects to see again) cost and bring in, in one call, without arguments. totals: monthlyCostCents and yearlyCostCents are the expenses (negative cents), monthlyIncomeCents the incomes (positive), activeCount the series that have not ended; an ended series (endsOn past) is listed but left out of the totals. Amounts are signed integer cents, divide by 100 to speak them: say "38,47 € par mois", never the raw cents. operations[]: id, label, category, account, period, dayRule, referenceAmountCents, monthlyCostCents, yearlyCostCents, currency, nextOccurrenceOn (the next due date not yet settled by a transaction, null once ended), lastAttachedOn, attachmentCount, and lastOccurrence (the latest transaction attached, with its dateGapDays and the deviations it carried: late, early, amount_up, amount_down). missedOccurrence is set when the latest due date is past its date tolerance with no transaction attached ("the rent did not come this month"), with occurrenceOn and daysOverdue; it is a fact to report, never a reason to alarm. priceChange (previousCents, currentCents, percent, since) is set when the amount the series is paid at moved from the one before by more than the series' amount tolerance. proposals[] are the attachments still waiting for the user's yes, each with its reason (late, early, amount_up, amount_down, ambiguous): confirm one with manage_operations attach. To create, change or delete a series use manage_operations.

get_reference_salary.name: get_reference_salary
get_reference_salary.description: Read the reference salary: the stable monthly salary the user's month is judged on, bonuses excluded, rather than what actually came in this month (a salary can arrive late, or two at once). No arguments. monthlyCents is positive integer cents, divide by 100 to speak it ("4 950 € par mois"); it is null when nothing is known, and then never say 0 €: say no salary is set yet, and that declaring it on the safety cushion or creating the recurring income operation "Salaire" fixes that. source says where it comes from, always say it: declared (the net salary the user declared on the safety cushion, it wins), expected (the expected amount of the recurring income operations in the "Salaire" category), measured (the average of their last 12 attached payments, for a recurring operation whose amount is measured), unknown. operations[] lists the salary recurring operations (id, label, categoryName, period, referenceAmountCents, monthlyCents brought to a month, source, paymentCount); two employers are two recurring operations, added. To change the salary use manage_safety_cushion or manage_operations.

get_savings_advances.name: get_savings_advances
get_savings_advances.description: Read the savings advances: what the user took from a savings or investment account to his checking account while his salary was late, and what is left to give back to each source ("combien je dois remettre sur mon livret ?"). No arguments. advances[] lists each one, oldest first: id, sourceAccountId, sourceAccountName, amountCents (avancé), openedOn, repaidCents (rendu), outstandingCents (reste à rendre), isClosed. bySource[] adds up what is left per source (sourceAccountId, sourceAccountName, outstandingCents, openCount), largest first; totalOutstandingCents is the total left to give back. A settled advance stays in advances[], closed, and leaves the totals. salaryDelay is the salary delay as manage_treasury_settings reports it. Amounts are positive integer cents, divide by 100 to speak them. Nothing here moves money: say what to transfer, never that it was transferred.

get_seasonal_produce.name: get_seasonal_produce
get_seasonal_produce.description: List the fruits and vegetables in season in metropolitan France for a month (1 = January … 12 = December; default: the current month in the user's timezone), from the seasonality calendar, and the user's own products in season that month. Use it to suggest seasonal meals or to say what is in season. To change the season of one of the user's products, use manage_products (seasonMonths).

get_tasks.name: get_tasks
get_tasks.description: Get tasks filtered by status. Status: pending (not done), done, overdue (past due date and not done), all. Optional days parameter limits upcoming scope. Tasks come highest orderScore first (done: most recently done first): cite them in that order. A view (given, status is ignored) is one tab of the task screen, each task in exactly one: "today" = not done, due today or late, by orderScore, each followed by its subtasks; "upcoming" = not done, due after today, by due day then orderScore; "someday" = not done, no due day, by priority then position; "done" = the 50 most recently done (total gives how many). counts gives the size of the four views. Use view "today" whenever the user asks about their day, their tasks or what is on: the late tasks and the urgent ones come first, already ranked by orderScore, so cite them in that order — late (overdueDays) before the others. Use view "someday" only to suggest a task to plan on a light day (few events, no high or critical urgency in today): it has no due day, so it is never late and never urgent by itself. Each task has urgency (low, normal, high, critical — computed from criticality and the due day, never set), orderScore (time pressure + criticality + priority), overdueDays (days late, null when not late) and parentId (the task it is a subtask of, or null), position (its order among its siblings, compared as a string), links (read from Google) and dueDate as YYYY-MM-DD.

get_treasury_outlook.name: get_treasury_outlook
get_treasury_outlook.description: Read the treasury until the salary comes ("je vais être à découvert ?", "combien je dois avancer ?"): the salary delay, the projected checking balance, the overdraft ahead and how much to advance from which savings. Optional months (1 to 12, a year at most; default: to the end of the month after the expected salary) sets how far it projects — computed on demand, nothing is stored. It only reads what is entered — the balances of the checking accounts, their planned and committed movements to come, and the occurrences the owner's confirmed recurring series still expect that no line is attached to yet — no average, no guess: every figure can be recomputed by hand, say so if asked. salary: isConfigured (false when no expected day or no reference salary is known: then nothing is projected and nothing is late — say so instead of saying all is fine), expectedOn (the salary awaited; in the past when late), referenceCents, isReceived (this month's salary is in), isLate, delayDays, shortfallCents. balanceCents is today's checking balance. projection[] gives, day by day from today to the horizon, date, balanceCents, cumulativeInflowCents and cumulativeOutflowCents (what came in and what went out since today, both as positive amounts, so the gap between them can be drawn — report them as figures, give no verdict) and the movements of the day (id, label, amountCents, status planned, committed or expected, source transaction or recurring, accountId, accountName; source recurring, status expected is a debit or credit of a confirmed recurring series that nothing is attached to yet — id is then the series', say it comes from the series, not from a line entered). balanceBeforeSalary {onDate, balanceCents} is the balance the eve of the salary, expenses of the salary day included (when late, today's end-of-day balance, after today's movements): use it, never recompute it. overdraft: isForecast, onDate (the first day of the whole projection below minus limitCents; today when already below), worstBalanceCents, limitCents (the overdraft the bank allows, set with manage_treasury_settings). advice, null when no overdraft is forecast: amountCents (what is missing to stay above the limit), sourceAccountId, sourceAccountName, sourceAmountCents (what to take from it) from the savings with the largest balance; alternatives[] (accountId, accountName, balanceCents, amountCents, isCushion) when it is not enough; uncoveredCents, what no source covers. A cushion account comes last: when isCushion or touchesCushion is true, say it breaks into the safety net and starts a recharge plan. outstandingAdvancesCents is what is still to give back from earlier advances (get_savings_advances for the detail). Amounts are integer cents, divide by 100 to speak them. Nothing here moves money: propose the transfer, never say it was made.

get_upcoming_events.name: get_upcoming_events

agendas.description: names or ids of the agendas to read

get_upcoming_events.description: Get upcoming events for the next N days (default 7). Returns events from all of the user agendas, including expanded recurring events. A whole-day event (allDay true) has no startAt/endAt but startDate, endDate EXCLUDED as in Google's API (the day after its last day) and lastDay: tell the user « le 1er janvier » or « du 26 au 28 » from startDate to lastDay, never « jusqu'au » endDate. Every local date comes with its day of the week (startWeekday, endWeekday for a timed event; startWeekday and lastDayWeekday for a whole-day one): say the weekday from those fields or from the date_time tool (weekday action), never work it out yourself. Pass agendas (a list of agenda names as the user says them — case, accents and approximations do not matter — or ids) whenever the user asked to be told only about some agendas (« ne me parle que de Défaut et Garde Ael », a rule to apply to every read from then on): only their events come back, and a name matching no agenda returns an error listing the user's agendas and no events at all. Omit it to read every agenda. Each event carries the name of its agenda (agenda) and its times in its own time zone (timeZone): announce those. To find an event by its name — before deleting or moving it, or before saying it does not exist — pass query, the distinctive word(s) of its title (case, accents and typos do not matter), and no days: the search then covers the next year, not a week; a recurring series comes back once, as its master event (id, rrule, first coming occurrence in startAt). Never conclude that an event does not exist from a short window; pass that id to update_event or delete_event.

get_upcoming_projection.name: get_upcoming_projection
get_upcoming_projection.description: Read what is coming ("qu'est-ce qui arrive la semaine prochaine ?", "que me restera-t-il le mois prochain ?"): the week after this one (Monday to Sunday) and the month after this one, projected from what is entered. date is optional, a day as YYYY-MM-DD (today by default): the week and the month are the ones after it. Nothing is extrapolated: only the occurrences the owner's confirmed recurring series still expect that no line is attached to, and the planned and committed movements on the open checking accounts; transfers between accounts are left out. week and month each give from and until (until is excluded), incomeCents (the expected income, the salary included when it is a confirmed series), expenseCents, netCents, incomes[] and expenses[] ({date, label, amountCents signed, source recurring, planned or committed, categoryId, categoryName}) and days[] ({date, incomeCents, expenseCents}) for a chart. month adds the envelopes as adjusted for that month: envelopes[] ({envelopeId, categoryId, categoryName, categoryPath, amountCents, committedCents, projectedCents, isOvercommitted}) for the top-level monthly envelopes — amountCents is the amount written for the month (its own envelope, else the month under way rolled over; a suggestion from envelope_adjustments that was not applied weighs nothing), committedCents what recurring and planned expenses already fill in its categories, projectedCents the greater of the two. envelopesCents is their sum, unbudgetedCents the commitments outside every envelope, projectedExpenseCents the two together and remainingCents the expected income less that spending: what is left to put toward the projects, negative when the month is short — say so, and name isOvercommitted envelopes. Annual and one-off envelopes are not part of a month. Project tracking is not here yet. Amounts are integer cents, divide by 100 to speak them. A pure read.

get_user_timezone.name: get_user_timezone
get_user_timezone.description: Read the IANA timezone (e.g. Europe/Paris) the user chose in their preferences. Use it to reason about the user's local time.

get_weather.name: get_weather
get_weather.description: Daily weather forecast from Open-Meteo: min and max temperature (°C), rain (mm and probability), wind and gusts (km/h), and alerts. Without `date` it returns today and tomorrow; with `date` (YYYY-MM-DD, from today up to 15 days ahead) only that day. `location` is a city name; without it the city the user chose in their preferences is used, and if there is none the tool says so — ask the user for a city. Alerts are derived from the forecast (storm, strong wind, heavy rain, snow, heat, hard frost), not official warnings. When the weather service is down the result is an `error`: say so plainly and carry on without the weather.

list_past_errands.name: list_past_errands
list_past_errands.description: Past errands (« courses passées »), most recent first: what the user bought, where and when — e.g. « qu'est-ce que j'ai acheté la dernière fois chez Carrefour ? » is store="Carrefour", limit=1. Each errand is one store (storeName, null when the lines had none), endedAt (ISO 8601) and its items: label, quantity, unit, product (IRI, null for a free-text line) and the packaging the product had then (packagingUnit, packagingSize, packagingSizeUnit, null when unknown). store matches the store name in part, case-insensitively; limit is 1 to 20 (5 by default). An errand is archived by end_errand.

list_proactions.name: list_proactions
list_proactions.description: List the proactions Maggie scheduled for the user, by time: each with its prompt, scheduledAt and status (pending, running, completed with its response, failed with its error). Optional from and to (ISO 8601, or YYYY-MM-DD for a whole day, read in Europe/Paris) bound scheduledAt; optional status filters. Use it before scheduling, so as not to schedule one that already exists.

list_routines.name: list_routines
list_routines.description: Read the user's routines — small habits that come back (a glass of water at waking, the bins on Tuesday evening). Without date: every routine, active or not, in the order of the day, as {routines: [...]}. With date (YYYY-MM-DD): only the active routines due that day, grouped by moment of the day, as {date, moments: [{anchor, time, routines: [...]}]}, each with checked (ticked that day or not). A routine has id, title, anchor (wake, afterBreakfast, afterLunch, afterDinner or time), anchorTime (HH:MM, only with anchor time), time (the hour it falls at), recurrence ({kind: daily} | {kind: weekdays} | {kind: weekly, weekday: 1 Monday to 7 Sunday} | {kind: monthly, monthDay: 1 to 31}), active, remind, createdAt, checkedToday, dueToday, monthCount (ticks this month) and totalCount (ticks since the creation). Report what was done — the month's count, the total — never a streak, never days missed.

manage_accounts.name: manage_accounts
manage_accounts.description: List, create, update, or delete bank accounts. An account has a name, bank, type (checking, savings, investment, cash), currency (ISO 4217), a balance in cents, and an optional cushion flag (emergency-fund account). Amounts are always in integer cents. On update, only provided fields change; to empty the optional bank, list it in clear.

manage_agendas.name: manage_agendas
manage_agendas.description: List, create, update, or delete agendas (calendars). An agenda has a name, description, IANA time zone, colour, and a default flag. Events always belong to an agenda. On update, to empty an optional field, list its name in clear (description, color). An agenda connected to Google is renamed in Google too: if Google cannot take the new name, the update fails with an error and the agenda keeps its name.

manage_aisles.name: manage_aisles
manage_aisles.description: List, create, update (rename and/or move), reorder or delete the aisles of a store. Aisles are the shelves of one store in the order the user walks through it (position 1 = first); the grocery list shows each store's items aisle by aisle in that order, items without an aisle last. list/create/reorder need storeId; update/delete need aisleId. create puts the aisle last unless position says where. reorder takes aisleIds: every aisle of the store, first one first. Deleting an aisle leaves its products without an aisle in that store. To put a product in an aisle, use assign_product_store.

manage_categories.name: manage_categories
manage_categories.description: List, create, update, or delete budget categories. Categories form a tree of at most three levels (Loisirs › Bars › Obsydian): a category may have a parentId, which may itself be a level-2 category; a level-3 category cannot have children, a category cannot move under its own descendants, and moving one never pushes its sub-categories past level 3. Each category is read with its depth (1 to 3) and its path (names from the top, joined by « › »). Each category has an obligation flag, deprecated: what a line is (mandatory, saving, repayment…) is now its own qualification, set on the transaction or the operation (manage_transactions, manage_operations: mandatory and kind). No calculation reads it any more (the score, the envelopes, the review and the lifestyle read the qualification of each transaction); it only gives the qualification a new line takes from its category until it goes: mandatory, optional, saving, investment, debt (loan repayments) or income. An income category may also be flagged passiveIncome: a rente, money that comes in without being worked for (rent received, dividends, interest, royalties) — that flag is what the independence counter counts, and it is refused on anything but an income category. On update, only provided fields change; to empty an optional field (make it a top-level category, drop its color or icon), list parentId, color or icon in clear.

manage_contacts.name: manage_contacts
manage_contacts.description: The people the owner lends money to or borrows from — one list for both — and the labels under which each one appears on the bank statements (counterparties, e.g. « VIR. DE TOM MARTIN »). Actions: list (every contact with its counterparties), search (by name, query), create (name, optional notes), update (contactId; only provided fields change; to empty notes, list it in clear), delete (contactId; their transactions are detached), link_counterparty (contactId and either label or transactionId — the label of that transaction is used; every non-internal transaction it recognises, past and future, is attached to the contact; a label belongs to one contact only), unlink_counterparty (counterpartyId; its transactions are detached), suggest_counterparties (contactId; labels of unattached transactions that contain a word of the name, most frequent first — confirm them with link_counterparty). A transfer between the owner's own accounts is never attached to a contact.

manage_envelopes.name: manage_envelopes
manage_envelopes.description: List, set, update, split or delete budget envelopes, and read the budget status of a period. An envelope budgets one category for one period: mode monthly needs year + month (1-12), mode annual needs year only (a calendar year, kept apart from the month's budget). Mode one_off is an event (Hellfest 2026, a trip) with a name and an amount but neither category nor period: set creates it from name + amountCents, and a spend is attributed to it by hand with manage_transactions (oneOffEnvelopeId), after which it keeps its category but counts in the one-off envelope only. amountCents is a positive integer amount in cents. The set action creates the envelope or updates the existing one for that category and period. The status action reports, per envelope, what is spent, committed, planned and to arbitrate, plus what is consumed (spent + committed), remaining and available (remaining minus planned); it defaults to the current month. Each envelope counts the transactions of its category and of every sub-category below it (an envelope is never compulsory: a spend on Loisirs › Bars › Obsydian counts in the envelope of Obsydian and in that of Loisirs, whichever of them exist), carries categoryPath and parentEnvelopeId (the envelope of its closest ancestor category, null for a root), and the totals only add the root envelopes. budgets and the totals are the monthly envelopes only; outsideMonthlyBudget lists apart the annual envelopes of the year (annual) and every one-off envelope with what was attributed to it (oneOff). The rollover action copies the envelopes of one period onto another (fromYear/fromMonth to year/month), keeping the same amounts unless useActualSpending is true, in which case each new envelope is budgeted on what its category actually consumed; envelopes already set on the target period are left untouched. The split action shares the amount of a mother envelope (envelopeId) between its daughters — the envelopes of its direct sub-categories for the same period — in one go: children is a list of {envelopeId, amountCents}; a daughter not listed keeps her amount, and what the daughters do not hold stays free in the mother (status reports allocatedToChildrenCents and freeCents for a mother). A split whose daughters would hold more than the mother is refused and changes nothing; the answer carries the current state. seasonalAmounts (monthly only, on set and update) gives a monthly envelope an amount per stretch of the year: a list of {fromMonth, toMonth, amountCents}, months 1-12, a season may cross the new year (Cinéma 45 € from November to February is {fromMonth: 11, toMonth: 2, amountCents: 4500}), two seasons never share a month; amountCents is then the amount of the months no season covers (20 € the rest of the year), a month a season covers is budgeted at the season's amount (monthAmountCents, and amountCents in status, whose season names it), and rollover carries the seasons over so each new month lands at its season's amount. Passing seasonalAmounts replaces every season; [] removes them.

manage_ingredients.name: manage_ingredients
manage_ingredients.description: Create, update, or delete food ingredients. Categories: produce, dairy, meat, fish, grain, spice, condiment, frozen, beverage, other. Units: g, kg, ml, l, cl, piece, bunch, can, bottle, pack, sachet, jar. Packaging is what the product is bought in: packagingUnit (pack, jar, bottle…), and optionally its content packagingSize + packagingSizeUnit, always together — a 500 g pack is packagingUnit=pack, packagingSize=500, packagingSizeUnit=g; a jar of unknown content is packagingUnit=jar alone. Call search_ciqual_foods first for nutrition data and pass the ciqualAlimCode; use search_ingredients to look one up. Stock: stockState says what is left at home — in_stock (default), low or out; restockQuantity is how many packagings to buy when it runs out (a whole number, 0 or more); autoRestock (true/false) puts it back on the list by itself. To empty an optional field on update, list its name in clear (defaultUnit, ciqualAlimCode, kcalPer100g, proteinPer100g, carbsPer100g, fatPer100g, packagingUnit, packagingSize, packagingSizeUnit, restockQuantity).

manage_loans.name: manage_loans
manage_loans.description: List, create, update or delete loans being repaid, and read the debt timeline. A loan is described by its remaining capital, its monthly payment and its annual rate in BASIS POINTS (350 = 3.50 %); the end date is never given, it is computed from those three. A payment that does not cover the monthly interest is refused, since such a loan would never be repaid. The timeline action amortises every loan month by month over a horizon (60 months by default) and reports when each one frees up, how much monthly payment that releases, and the net saving capacity — reference income minus loan payments minus the lifestyle measured over the last three months. All amounts are integer cents. On update, only provided fields change; to empty the optional lender, list it in clear.

manage_meal_groceries.name: manage_meal_groceries
manage_meal_groceries.description: Choose which ingredients of a planned meal go on the grocery list. preview lists the meal's ingredients with the quantity to buy in packagings (toBuy), the product's stock state (in_stock, low, out) and suggested=true when it is low or out: tell the owner which ones are running low and ask which to add. add puts only the chosen ones on the list, in packagings, and replaces what the meal had put there before: ingredientIds is a comma-separated list of ingredientId from preview, empty to add nothing.

manage_meal_settings.name: manage_meal_settings
manage_meal_settings.description: Read or change the meal settings. defaultGuests is how many people a meal is cooked for when it names no guests of its own (1 or more, 2 until the user sets it). Action get returns the settings; action update sets defaultGuests, which is required, and rescales on the grocery list what the meals still to come that follow the default had put there — a meal with its own guests keeps them.

manage_meals.name: manage_meals
manage_meals.description: List, plan, update, or delete meals. A meal is a day and a slot, never a time: date, fromDate and toDate are YYYY-MM-DD with no hour, slot is lunch or dinner, and recipeIds is a comma-separated list. List needs fromDate and toDate. create answers groceryPreview: the meal's ingredients with their stock, to choose from with manage_meal_groceries add. guests is how many people the meal is cooked for (1 or more): the recipes' quantities scale to it, and changing it on update rescales what the meal put on the grocery list. Without guests a meal follows the user's default (manage_meal_settings); useDefaultGuests true on update gives it back to the default. Every meal answered carries guests and guestsIsDefault.

manage_notifications.name: manage_notifications
manage_notifications.description: Create, list, mark as read, or delete notifications. Use create to reach the user on their own devices (push notification): a proaction you took or an approval you are waiting for — type is one of proaction, approval, reminder, task_due, grocery, finance; give a short title, an optional body, and relatedEntityIri (e.g. /api/events/{id}, /api/tasks/{id}, /finance/banks) so tapping it opens the right screen. Use unreadOnly to see what still needs attention.

manage_operations.name: manage_operations
manage_operations.description: List, create, update or delete the operations, preview what one would catch, apply them to the history, learn one from a transaction, and attach or detach the transactions of a series. An operation is what recognises the transactions (the real lines of the statement) and the qualification it copies onto each of them (categoryId, mandatory, kind), with an optional recurrence: with one it is a series the user expects to see again (rent on the 5th, a subscription on the 12th, a salary), without one it files lines like a categorization rule. Recognition: counterpartyName (who the bank names, the main way: copy the counterpartyName of a transaction as the bank spells it), labelPattern read in the label (matchType: contains, starts_with, equals — case-insensitive), and the amount. Without a counterparty or a label, the amount alone recognises: a series by its sign and referenceAmountCents within amountTolerancePercent, an operation without recurrence by direction (debit = expense, credit = income) with minAmountCents and/or maxAmountCents (ABSOLUTE cents: a 15,99 € expense matches 1000..2000; « an income of 4 750 € ± 10 % is the salary »: direction credit, minAmountCents 427500, maxAmountCents 522500, compute the bounds yourself); with nothing to recognise by, it is refused with the current state. The recurrence is period (weekly, monthly, quarterly, yearly), anchorOn (ISO date of the first occurrence; every other one is counted from it), referenceAmountCents (signed integer cents, never 0: negative = expense, positive = income) and accountId (its currency is the account's), all four together or none — a part of them is refused — with a label, and optionally dayRule (fixed_day: the anchor's day, clamped to short months; last_day_of_month), referenceSource (measured: follows the attached transactions, the default; declared: stays as typed), amountTolerancePercent (0-100, 20 by default), dateToleranceDays (0-31, 5 by default) and endsOn (ISO date, not before anchorOn). An operation keeps its recurrence or its lack of one: to change, create another. Order of a new line: internal transfers and rejected payments are set aside, then the series attach the lines of their occurrences, then the first active operation without recurrence by priority (highest first; isActive false pauses one) files what is left; a line the user qualified by hand is never overwritten. Any category fits any sign. List gives every operation (recurring true or false narrows it) with, for a series, monthlyCostCents, yearlyCostCents and nextOccurrenceOn (after today). On update, only provided fields change; to remove label, counterpartyName, labelPattern, minAmountCents, maxAmountCents or endsOn, list it in clear; a new categoryId, mandatory or kind reaches every transaction the operation qualified, except those the user qualified by hand. BEFORE creating an operation, call action preview with the same criteria: without referenceAmountCents it is an operation without recurrence's (total, changeCount: the lines it would re-file, the latest matches; pass operationId when editing a saved one), with it a series' (the lines it would recognise, optionally on accountId). Show the user what it found, then ask whether to apply it to the existing transactions: create and update take applyToExisting (default false: only the lines to come). apply with an operationId gives the history to that one; without, it runs the whole catch-up (the series attach, then the others file). learn turns transactionId into an operation without recurrence filing under categoryId what has the same label (labelPattern derived from it unless given), and files that line by hand. attach makes transactionId an occurrence of the series operationId, by hand: at recurringOccurrenceOn (ISO date, a due date of the series), or at the due date nearest its bookedAt; it is how the user confirms a proposed attachment (late, early, amount_up for a price rise, amount_down, ambiguous). It is refused when the occurrence is already settled by another transaction (detach that one first), or when the account, the currency or the sign differ. detach takes transactionId out of its series for good. Both are recorded as the user's own decision, which the automatic attachment never overwrites; a measured reference amount follows the latest attachments. Attaching gives the line the whole qualification of the series, unless the user qualified it by hand. mandatory (true or false: an obligation the user cannot cut) and kind (none, saving, investment, loan or repayment: the direction is the sign of the amount, a repayment is « I pay back » on a debit and « I am paid back » on a credit) qualify the lines, with the category: give them together, or neither — one without the other is refused with the current qualification. Without them, a new categoryId brings the qualification of the category.

manage_peer_debts.name: manage_peer_debts

shares.description: what the agent sent: checked one by one

manage_peer_debts.description: Money between the owner and the people around them (créances: they owe the owner; dettes: the owner owes them). Not bank loans (manage_loans). Actions: list (every créance and dette, newest first, each with its shares per person — contactId, contactName, amountCents, repaidCents, remainingCents —, amountCents, remainingCents and status open or settled; optional contactId to keep those of one person, optional status open or settled, optional direction owed_to_me or i_owe; each also carries history: the transfers that gave it back — transactionId, bookedAt, label, amountCents, contactId, contactName), summary (owedToMeCents: what people still owe the owner, iOweCents: what the owner still owes, byContact: per person with something left — contactId, name, netCents, positive when they owe the owner, negative when the owner owes them —, compensates: true when they owe each other, one transfer of the difference settles both), set_my_share (a spend paid for others too, e.g. a 800 € gîte for four: transactionId, myShareCents — the owner's own part, 0 ≤ part < the amount; only it counts in the envelopes, the score, the review and the lifestyle —, shares: [{contactId, amountCents}] — the people who owe the rest, contacts from manage_contacts; leave every amountCents out to split equally, or give them all adding up to the amount minus the part —, optional object (what it was for, the label by default) and notes; setting it again updates the same créance; myShareCents null removes the share and its créance, refused once someone gave money back on it). Only a spend can be shared, not an income nor an internal transfer. record_debt (a transfer received that must be given back in part, e.g. Tom advances 400 € of which 280 € are his: transactionId — a received transfer, neither a spend nor an internal transfer —, contactId — the person it comes from, the transaction's contact is the natural one —, amountCents — what to give back, 0 < amount ≤ the transfer —, optional object and notes) records a dette (direction i_owe, one share) that is neither an income nor a saving: the rest of the transfer stays an income; declaring it again updates the same dette; amountCents null removes it, refused once part of it was given back. allocate (what a transfer with a person is — transactionId, kind: for a received transfer income (all of it stays an income), repayment (it gives back créances) or new_debt (money to give back: contactId, amountCents, optional object and notes, like record_debt); for a sent transfer repayment (it gives back dettes), new_claim (money lent: a créance of the whole amount to contactId, optional object and notes) or other (a plain spend). One allocation per call: for repayment give shareId — a share from list, of a créance for a received transfer, of a dette for a sent one, those of the transfer's contact first — and amountCents, at most what is left on that share; the transfer's other allocations are kept, amountCents 0 takes that share off, and all of them add up to at most the transfer. What is not allocated of a received transfer stays an income. An allocated part is neither an income nor a spend. kind null undoes the answer and gives back what it repaid. Never an internal transfer.) Returns the transfer's peerKind, allocations, unallocatedCents and the candidate shares.

manage_period_plan.name: manage_period_plan
manage_period_plan.description: Write one element of the plan of a period, once the owner has decided it (read the plan first with plan_annual_budget, which takes the same period). period is a year (2027), a quarter (2027-Q2) or a semester (2027-S1). One call writes one element; repeat the call for the next one. Actions: set_annual_envelope (categoryId, amountCents; the period must be a year) sets the annual envelope of a category; set_monthly_envelope (categoryId, amountCents) sets the same monthly envelope on every month of the period, and seasonFromMonth + seasonToMonth + seasonAmountCents together (1-12) give those months of the year another amount — one season per call, which replaces the seasons of those envelopes; set_one_off_envelope (name, amountCents) sets the envelope of an event with no category, found by its name; set_event (categoryId, label, amountCents, month as YYYY-MM inside the period, optional accountId) plans an expense, booked on the 15th of that month on the first checking account unless accountId says otherwise. amountCents is positive, in cents; currency defaults to EUR. Replaying a call updates what it wrote and never duplicates; an expense the owner already committed is left alone. The envelopes and planned expenses written are the plan: nothing else is stored, and the calendar is never touched.

manage_products.name: manage_products
manage_products.description: List, create, update, or delete non-food products (household, hygiene, cleaning, other). Create food items with manage_ingredients instead — they are products too, so they show up in the list. To search by name use search_products. Units: g, kg, ml, l, cl, piece, bunch, can, bottle, pack, sachet, jar. Packaging is what the product is bought in: packagingUnit (pack, jar, bottle…), and optionally its content packagingSize + packagingSizeUnit, always together — a 500 g pack is packagingUnit=pack, packagingSize=500, packagingSizeUnit=g; a jar of unknown content is packagingUnit=jar alone. Stock: stockState says what is left at home — in_stock (default), low or out; restockQuantity is how many packagings to buy when it runs out (a whole number, 0 or more); autoRestock (true/false) puts it back on the list by itself. Season: seasonMonths lists the months (1 = January … 12 = December) a fruit or vegetable is in season in metropolitan France; it is pre-filled from the seasonality calendar on create when the name is known, and inSeason says whether the product is in season this month (null: no season). To empty an optional field on update, list its name in clear (defaultUnit, packagingUnit, packagingSize, packagingSizeUnit, restockQuantity, seasonMonths).

manage_projects.name: manage_projects
manage_projects.description: List, create, update, delete or reorder the user's projects — the things they save for (a trip, a move, a sofa). A project has a name, amountCents (what it costs, integer cents, > 0), currency (3-letter code, EUR by default), wellbeing (how much it counts for the user: essential = score 4, high = 3, medium = 2 (default), comfort = 1; read back as wellbeingScore), dateMode and targetOn (ISO date YYYY-MM-DD): none = no date, movable, the planning will place it (targetOn must be absent); fixed = a locked date the user cannot move (a wedding, moving house); deadline = done at the latest on targetOn. fixed and deadline require targetOn. dependsOn is the list of the user's project ids this one waits for (it replaces the whole list; a project cannot depend on itself, nor close a cycle A → B → A). note is free text. position is the priority order, 0 = highest priority: a new project goes last, only reorder changes it, with ids = EVERY project id of the user in the new order (a partial list is refused with the current order). unmetDependencies lists the ids of the dependencies whose date this project does not respect: both are dated and this one comes before the one it waits for. Nothing is ever deduced: create needs name and amountCents; a dateMode fixed or deadline needs targetOn, a targetOn needs a dateMode fixed or deadline; on update only provided fields change, and switching a dated project to none needs targetOn in clear. A refused request answers error plus current (what was given, or the project as it is now). clear empties note, dependsOn or targetOn.

manage_recurring_groceries.name: manage_recurring_groceries
manage_recurring_groceries.description: List, create, update, or delete recurring grocery items — the staples automatically added to generated lists. Frequency: weekly, biweekly, monthly. Give either a productId or a customLabel. To empty an optional field on update, list its name in clear (productId, customLabel, quantity, unit); an item must keep a productId or a customLabel.

manage_safety_cushion.name: manage_safety_cushion
manage_safety_cushion.description: Read or configure the safety cushion — the emergency fund that must be full before any investment or project starts. The status action reports its state (building, complete, recharging), its target (targetMonths x monthly net income), what the cushion currently holds (the balance of the cushion accounts less peerClaimsCents, what friends and family still owe the owner — it fills back up with every repayment; a debt the owner owes never raises it), the deficit, and the monthly recharge plan. Its current amount is never set by hand: it is the balance of the accounts flagged as cushion. The configure action sets targetMonths, monthlyNetIncomeCents, rechargeCapCents (the most that may go back in per month) and rechargeTargetMonths (the wished-for recharge horizon; when the cap is lower, the recharge simply takes longer). All amounts are integer cents.

manage_stores.name: manage_stores
manage_stores.description: List, create, update, or delete stores. Stores represent shops with a visit order and a description of what they sell (used to auto-assign products). To empty an optional field on update, list its name in clear (description).

manage_transactions.name: manage_transactions
manage_transactions.description: List, create, update, delete, or categorize transactions; to_sort and sort work through the pile of lines that still wait for a category. List returns the newest first, one page at a time (limit, 30 by default, 100 at most) with total, the number of lines matching in all: to look further back or for something precise, narrow with categoryId (the category and its sub-categories; with limit 1, the latest line of that category), direction (expense or income), fromDate and toDate (ISO dates, both included), accountId, or query (text found in the label or in the counterparty, i.e. the creditor or debtor the bank names) instead of asking for more. List leaves the rejected payments out (a rejected debit and the credit that gave it back, which the account page shows apart as incidents): pass transferKind rejected to list only them, e.g. to count the direct debits rejected this month (each rejection is two lines, the debit and the credit), or internal or none to list only those (advance, repayment and funding each list only their own). Each line carries its label and its counterpartyName. Amounts are signed integer cents: negative = expense/debit, positive = income/credit; any category may be used on either sign. bookedAt is an ISO date (defaults to today). status is one of spent, committed, planned, to_arbitrate. On update, only provided fields change; to remove the category, list categoryId in clear. transferKind says whether the line is a neutral movement. internal is a movement between two of the user's own accounts, with counterpartId naming the other leg (omit it when only one of the two accounts is known), or none to take it back out of the transfers — list transferKind in clear for the same effect. transferKind rejected marks a payment the bank rejected, with counterpartId naming the credit that gave it back on the same account (the detection pairs them as they arrive: a credit worded REJET, IMPAYE or RETOUR PRLV with the debit of the same payee and amount). transferKind advance is an internal transfer from a savings or investment account to a checking one made while the salary was late, which the detection marks (get_savings_advances says what is left to give back); repayment is the transfer that gives an advance back, from the checking account to the source: the detection marks it when its amount equals exactly what is left of an open advance of that source (a partial amount is never reconciled), and by hand it takes counterpartId plus repaysTransactionId, the id of the advance (the debit leg get_savings_advances lists), set on the debit leg, the one leaving the checking account. funding is the user's regular top-up of a savings account, which the detection never takes for a repayment whatever its amount: mark it with transferKind funding and counterpartId (or alone when only one account is known); it stays a neutral internal transfer. propose_advance_repayments says what to transfer to give the advances back. An internal transfer or a rejection counts neither as an expense nor as an income; transferNote says it in the words the user sees (« Virement interne », « Rejeté » on the rejected payment, « Rejet de … » on the credit). A marking made here is recorded as the user's own decision, which the detection never overwrites; detect_internal_transfers is what pairs a whole history. recurringOperationId names the recurring operation the line is an occurrence of, and recurringOccurrenceOn (ISO date) the due date it settles: a line is attached automatically when its counterparty, its date and its amount all match a free occurrence. On update, recurringOperationId attaches the line by hand (to recurringOccurrenceOn, or to the due date nearest its bookedAt), recurringOccurrenceOn alone moves it to another due date of its series, and recurringOperation in clear detaches it; a gesture made here is recorded as the user's own (recurringSource manual), which the automatic attachment never overwrites. Attaching gives the line the whole qualification of the recurring operation (categoryId, mandatory, kind), unless the user qualified it by hand. note is the user's free text about the line (2000 characters at most): set it on create or update, a blank note or note in clear removes it, and an update that omits it leaves it alone. oneOffEnvelopeId attributes a spend by hand to a one-off envelope (an event such as Hellfest 2026, created with manage_envelopes mode one_off): the line keeps its category but leaves the monthly and annual envelopes and counts in the one-off one only; an empty oneOffEnvelopeId or oneOffEnvelope in clear takes the attribution back. Action to_sort lists the lines to sort one by one (limit, 50 by default): no category and not a transfer or a rejection — reason category —, or a transfer with a contact not told apart yet — reason peer_transfer, asksForPeerKind true: answer it with manage_peer_debts allocate —, newest first, with total and, on each, a suggestion {categoryId, categoryPath, source rule|merchant, reason} or null. Action sort answers one of them: transactionId plus categoryId (the category is set by hand; alwaysForMerchant true also writes a 'contains' rule on the first words of the label and files the other lines of the pile it claims) or transferKind internal (optional counterpartId) when the line moves money between the user's own accounts; a line that already has a category or a marking is refused. Action settle_rejection (transactionId: either leg of a rejected payment) records that the user dealt with it (paid again by other means), so it leaves the account incidents, the pile of rejections still to deal with; unsettle_rejection puts it back; any other line is refused. Each line carries rejectionSettledAt (ISO date-time, null while unsettled). qualifiedBy says who qualified a line: manual (the user, by hand: what is set here), series (an operation with a recurrence, qualifiedBySeriesId) or rule (an operation without, qualifiedByRuleId); a change to that operation reaches the line, never once it is qualified by hand. retrospect is the owner's satisfaction with a spend, given once per line when it is reviewed: keep (« À conserver »), avoidable (« Superflue ») or unrated; set it on update, it is refused on an income or on a transfer between the user's own accounts. to_sort and sort also carry judgeable (true on a spend) and retrospect on each line, and to_sort totalCents, the sum of the amounts still to qualify. myShareCents is the owner's own part of a shared spend, null when it is not shared: only it counts in the envelopes — set it with manage_peer_debts set_my_share. peerKind is what a transfer with a person is (income, repayment, new_debt, new_claim, other; null until told apart) and peerAllocatedCents what it gives back of créances or dettes — neither an income nor a spend: set them with manage_peer_debts allocate. mandatory (true or false: an obligation the user cannot cut) and kind (none, saving, investment, loan or repayment: the direction is the sign of the amount, a repayment is « I pay back » on a debit and « I am paid back » on a credit) qualify the lines, with the category: give them together, or neither — one without the other is refused with the current qualification. Without them, a new categoryId brings the qualification of the category.

manage_treasury_settings.name: manage_treasury_settings
manage_treasury_settings.description: Read or change the treasury settings: salaryExpectedDay, the day of the month the salary is expected on (1 to 31; on a shorter month, its last day), and overdraftLimitCents, the overdraft the bank allows in positive integer cents (0, the default, means any negative balance is an overdraft; get_treasury_outlook only announces an overdraft below minus this limit). Action get returns the settings and salaryDelay; action update sets salaryExpectedDay and/or overdraftLimitCents — only what is given changes — or forgets the day with clearSalaryExpectedDay true. Setting the day does not look back by itself: offer to run detect_internal_transfers afterwards, which marks as advances the transfers from savings already made during a delay. salaryDelay says whether the salary is late, for the previous month and the current one: isConfigured is false when no expected day or no reference salary is known, and then nothing is late — say so instead of saying the salary is on time. The salary is late from the day after the expected day until the credits recognised as the salary reach 90 % of the reference salary — those in the « Salaire » category, or any other credit within 10 % of the reference booked from 5 days before the expected day on (however late it comes), except a bonus, a rente, a transfer, or a credit carrying the owner's own name; a bonus closes nothing. isLate, delayDays (days since the expected day of the oldest month still open) and shortfallCents (what is still missing, integer cents) sum it up; months[] gives month, expectedOn, receivedCents, referenceCents, isReceived, receivedOn, isDue, delayDays and shortfallCents.

manage_utensils.name: manage_utensils
manage_utensils.description: List, create, rename, or delete the user's kitchen utensils (oven, Thermomix, mandoline…), the catalogue recipes say they are made with. A name is unique whatever its case: create answers the existing utensil when the name is already there. Deleting a utensil removes it from its recipes, which stay.

monthly_review.name: monthly_review
monthly_review.description: Run the monthly look back over a month (defaults to the one just ended). The review action lists the non-mandatory spends still waiting for a verdict, biggest first, and reports how much was kept, how much was judged avoidable, an optimisation score (the share of the judged amount worth keeping, null when nothing has been judged yet), and how the month compares with the previous one, the average of the last three and the same month last year. The rate action records one verdict: keep, avoidable, or unrated to undo it. Only non-mandatory spends are offered — asking whether someone could have skipped their rent helps nobody.

move_to_fallback.name: move_to_fallback
move_to_fallback.description: When a store is closed, move all unchecked items from that store to their fallback stores.

plan_annual_budget.name: plan_annual_budget
plan_annual_budget.description: Run the yearly planning session: what the year behind cost, and what the year ahead should therefore be budgeted. Lists every category the year behind cost something, biggest decision first, and reports for each what it was budgeted and really consumed, its big expenses one by one (the debits over thresholdCents, 10000 by default — the threshold decides which expenses are listed, never which categories are in the session), what the target year has already planned and committed, what its confirmed recurring series still debit (recurringCents per category: the occurrences with no line attached, each counted once — a rent already booked is the line's, never counted twice; decidedCents is planned + committed + recurring), what is only to arbitrate (reported, never counted), the annual envelope already set, and a suggested amount: what the target year has already decided on if anything, otherwise what the year behind consumed. year is between 2000 and 2100 and defaults to the one being prepared, which is next year in November and December and the current one the rest of the time. This only reads; it writes nothing: once the owner has decided, set the amounts and the planned expenses with manage_period_plan, one element per call (manage_envelopes and manage_transactions still work for a single line). It never touches the calendar either: a planned expense is a transaction, not an appointment. period (2027, 2027-Q2 or 2027-S1) plans a quarter or a semester instead of a year, as the review of a quarter, semester or year end does: the period read is the one of the same length right before it, the budget of a period under a year is what its monthly envelopes add up to, and suggestedMonthlyCents is the suggestion per month. Do not send period and year together. To write the plan of a period, use manage_period_plan, one element per call.

prepare_day.name: prepare_day
prepare_day.description: Propose the user's day for the morning, writing nothing: up to 5 tasks chosen by a simple rule — slots already written for the day are kept, then the tasks put off (« reportée »), due that day, urgent, due the next day, the others by score — filled while their estimated minutes (15 when unknown) fit the free time of the agenda between the morning time and 21:00 (or now, when later), at least one, shortest first. date is YYYY-MM-DD, today (the user's timezone) when left out. Returns slots [{position, type, reason, minutes, task}], reserveRanked (the other open tasks, best first, to swap in: [{reason, minutes, task}]), totalMinutes and freeMinutes. reason is postponed, dueToday, urgent, dueTomorrow, quick or whenever. To settle the proposal call set_day_plan with the taskIds of the slots; nothing is written until then.

propose_advance_repayments.name: propose_advance_repayments
propose_advance_repayments.description: Say what to transfer to give the savings advances back ("quoi virer, où, et combien ?"). No arguments. One counter-transfer per open advance, of exactly what is left of it, from the checking account the money landed on to the savings source it came from: proposals[] gives fromAccountId, toAccountId, amountCents, advanceId, currency and a label ready to copy; totalCents adds them up. The proposal is capped at what the checking account holds: when it cannot cover an advance, the proposal is reduced to the balance (isPartial true) and unproposed[] says what could not be proposed (advanceId, sourceAccountName, amountCents, reason insufficient_balance or no_checking_account), unproposedCents adding it up — say it plainly, never present a reduced transfer as the full return. With no open advance, proposals is empty and that is good news: nothing is owed. Amounts are positive integer cents, divide by 100 to speak them. Nothing here moves money: say what to transfer, never that it was transferred. When the user makes the exact transfer, the next detection settles the advance on its own; a regular top-up of the savings account is never counted as a return (mark it funding with manage_transactions if it could be mistaken for one).

record_proaction_result.name: record_proaction_result
record_proaction_result.description: Reserved for the proaction executor — never call it in a conversation. Records how a claimed (running) proaction went: status completed with response (Maggie's message, may be empty), or status failed with error.

remove_grocery_item.name: remove_grocery_item
remove_grocery_item.description: Remove a specific item from the grocery list.

reorder_grocery_items.name: reorder_grocery_items
