reorder_grocery_items.description: Reorder grocery items by setting their position. Pass an array of {id, position} pairs.

save_routine.name: save_routine
save_routine.description: Create or change a routine — a small habit that comes back. Without id: creates it, and title, anchor and recurrence are all required (nothing is guessed: ask the user for what is missing). With id: changes only the fields given, the others stay as they are. title: what to do, 255 characters at most. anchor: the moment of the day it belongs to — wake, afterBreakfast, afterLunch, afterDinner — or time for a fixed hour, which needs anchorTime "HH:MM" (24 hours, user's timezone) and is the only anchor allowed one. recurrence: {kind: daily}, {kind: weekdays} (Monday to Friday), {kind: weekly, weekday: 1 Monday to 7 Sunday} (« le mardi » is weekday 2) or {kind: monthly, monthDay: 1 to 31} (a shorter month falls on its last day); weekday and monthDay go with their kind only. active=false pauses it without losing its ticks; remind=true asks for a reminder. A refused or incomplete call changes nothing and answers {error} with the routine as it stands (changing) or the fields given (creating). Returns {success, routine} as list_routines reads it. Deleting a routine is not possible from here: the user does it in the app.

schedule_proaction.name: schedule_proaction
schedule_proaction.description: Schedule ONE run of Maggie at a given moment: at scheduled_at, Maggie receives prompt as her instruction and acts — remind, check, report. It is filed as an event of the user's internal « Maggie » agenda (never synced with Google), five minutes long, so the user sees it and can move or delete it there. Choose between the two first: anything lasting or repeating (« tous les lundis », « les jours où j'ai Ael », « préviens-moi toujours… ») is an instruction — use add_instruction, never a proaction and never an RRULE; a single occurrence (« demain à 8 h 30 », « dans une heure ») is a proaction. scheduled_at is ISO 8601 with a time, e.g. 2037-01-15T08:30:00+01:00, read in Europe/Paris when it has no offset; it must be in the future. prompt is what Maggie will do, written for herself with everything she will need. summary is the short label shown in the agenda (optional, taken from the prompt). Returns the proaction as saved (proaction.scheduledAt): announce exactly that.

search.name: search
search.description: Full-text search across the user's own data stored in Maggie (events, tasks, recipes, products, grocery lists, notifications). Returns matching results with highlights, with no limit of date: to find an event by its name, pass types events. Bank transactions are not searched by default: to find a transaction, pass types=transactions or use the finance tools. Every event result carries the day of the week of its local dates (data.startWeekday, endWeekday for a timed event; startWeekday and lastDayWeekday for a whole-day one, whose endDate is EXCLUDED — lastDay is its last day): say the weekday from those fields or from the date_time tool, never work it out yourself. It does NOT search the Internet: for public facts (official dates, opening hours, addresses, news) use the web_search tool.

search_ciqual_foods.name: search_ciqual_foods
search_ciqual_foods.description: Search the Ciqual (ANSES) French food composition database by name. Returns foods with core macros (kcal, protein, carbs, fat per 100g). Use this to find nutrition data for ingredients.

search_ingredients.name: search_ingredients
search_ingredients.description: Search food ingredients by name. Returns matching ingredients with id, name, and category.

search_products.name: search_products
search_products.description: Search all products (food and non-food) by name. Returns matching products with id, name, category, and type.

search_recipes.name: search_recipes
search_recipes.description: Search recipes by name or tag. Provide either query (name search) or tag (tag search).

set_day_plan.name: set_day_plan
set_day_plan.description: Set the user's day: taskIds is the whole list of the day's tasks, in order, 5 at most — it replaces the slots, so to add one keep the others, and to put a task in place of another list it where the other was (the other goes back to the reserve). A task appears once. date is YYYY-MM-DD, today when left out; a future day can be written. confirm=false writes a proposal the user has not settled yet (confirmedAt stays null). Returns the day as get_day_plan does.

suggest_recurring_operations.name: suggest_recurring_operations
suggest_recurring_operations.description: Find the recurring operations the bank history implies (a subscription, the rent, a salary: the same payee coming back every week, month, quarter or year for a steady amount) and create the ones the user accepts. Action list reads and writes nothing: each suggestion has label, counterpartyName / counterpartyKey (who the bank names) or labelPattern (read in the label when there is no counterparty), accountId, accountName, period (weekly, monthly, quarterly, yearly), anchorOn (the first occurrence seen), dayRule (fixed_day or last_day_of_month), referenceAmountCents (signed integer cents, the median: negative is an expense; divide by 100 to speak it, say "13,49 € par mois", never the raw cents), amountSpreadPercent, occurrences, categoryId / categoryName (null when no heading is known: ask the user for one before accepting) and up to three samples. minOccurrences (default 3, at least 2) narrows the list. Present the suggestions in plain words ("Flixo revient le 12 de chaque mois, 13,49 €") and NEVER accept one without the user's explicit yes. Action accept takes suggestions: the chosen entries of the list, sent back as they were (categoryId filled in when null); an entry without a category, with a category or account that is not the user's, or whose payee already has a series is ignored. It creates the series and attaches the history they recognise, and answers created, labels, attached, proposed. Never suggest cancelling a subscription. Loan instalments and transfers between own accounts are never suggested. Each suggestion is an operation with a recurrence, in the shape manage_operations create takes; to change or delete it afterwards use manage_operations.

update_event.name: update_event

reminders.description: minutes before the start, e.g. [60] for "une heure avant"

update_event.description: Update an existing calendar event. When the user names the event rather than gives its id, find its id first with get_upcoming_events and query (the distinctive word(s) of its title, no days: it searches the next year) or search with types events — never conclude it does not exist from a 7-day window. A recurring series is designated by its master event, the id that search returns, not by one occurrence. Only provided fields will be updated. To change when it happens, always give the whole schedule — a start and an end, never a duration: start_date (YYYY-MM-DD) + start_time (HH:MM) + end_date + end_time, or for a whole-day event all_day true + start_date + end_date, where end_date is EXCLUDED — the day after the last day, as in Google Calendar's API: the 1st of January alone is start_date 2037-01-01 and end_date 2037-01-02, « du 26 au 28 janvier » is start_date the 26th and end_date the 29th. For "du X au Y", holidays, a trip or any stretch of several days, make ONE whole-day event with all_day true, start_date and end_date: never simulate a range with rrule (that makes one event per day) or with a long timed event. Nothing is deduced from the current schedule: moving an event to another day means giving its start and its end again. An incomplete schedule, or an end that is not after the start, changes nothing and returns an error with currentSchedule, the schedule the event has now — complete it from there instead of guessing. The result gives the schedule that was saved, in the event's own time zone (event.allDay; event.startAt and event.endAt for a timed event; for a whole-day event, whose startAt and endAt are null, event.startDate, event.endDate excluded and event.lastDay — tell the user the days it covers, « le 1er janvier » or « du 26 au 28 », from startDate to lastDay, never « jusqu'au » the excluded end): announce exactly that to the user, not what you meant to do. The result also gives the day of the week of what was saved (event.weekday, and startWeekday, endWeekday or lastDayWeekday next to each date): check that it is the day you announced to the user — « lundi 26 » must come back lundi — and if it is not, fix the event before confirming. Never work out a day of the week yourself: take it from these fields, from the weekday of a read tool, or from the date_time tool. Title, location, description, agenda and reminders change on their own, without touching the schedule. To empty an optional field, list its name in clear (description, location, rrule, reminders). Use agenda_id to move the event to another agenda: pass its name as the user said it (e.g. "Concerts", case and accents do not matter) or its id — no need to call manage_agendas first. An unknown or ambiguous name returns an error listing the user's agendas. Use status to mark the event 'tentative' ("provisoire", "à confirmer", "peut-être") or back to 'confirmed' ("confirme", "c'est validé"): it changes on its own, without touching the schedule, and event.status gives the status that was saved — say so when the event is tentative. Use reminders to replace the whole set of reminders: a list of delays in minutes before the start, e.g. [60] or [10, 1440]; it replaces what the event had, so pass every reminder the user wants to keep, and clear "reminders" to leave none.

update_recipe.name: update_recipe
update_recipe.description: Update an existing recipe. Only provided fields will be updated. Ingredients replaces the full list if provided. Each ingredient object needs quantity, unit, and either ingredientId or ciqualAlimCode. To empty an optional field, list its name in clear (notes); an empty tags string empties the tags. Utensils is a JSON array of what the recipe is made with, each a utensil id (from manage_utensils) or a name — a name not in the catalogue yet is added to it; it replaces the full list if provided, and [] empties it. The method goes in steps, notes keep the tips. Steps is a JSON array of the steps, in order (the first is step 1), each {text, durationMinutes?, background?, ingredientIds?, utensils?, waitsFor?}: ingredientIds names ingredients of the recipe by ingredientId or by name (only a link: a partial quantity goes in the text); utensils are utensil ids or names, added to the recipe's utensils; background (needs a duration) means the timer runs while the cook moves on; waitsFor lists the positions of earlier steps that must be finished first. Steps replaces the full list if provided, and [] empties it.

update_stock.name: update_stock
update_stock.description: Say what is left of a product at home: state is in_stock, low (nearly out) or out. Use it when the user says they are nearly out of something or have run out — not add_grocery_item. product is a product id or its name. When the product is set to restock by itself (autoRestock with a restockQuantity), its restock quantity is put on the grocery list for you and the answer says what was added; otherwise nothing is added and the answer says why. The answer also lists the meals of the next 7 days whose recipes use the product: tell the user about them.

update_task.name: update_task
update_task.description: Update an existing task. Only provided fields will be updated. Set done=true to mark as completed, done=false to reopen. Due date format: YYYY-MM-DD. parentId makes it a subtask of that task (one level only), position sets its order among its siblings. estimatedMinutes (1 to 1440) is how long it should take, firstStep the first small gesture that starts it; both stay in Maggie. To empty an optional field, list its name in clear (description, dueDate, parent — parent makes it a top-level task again —, estimatedMinutes, firstStep).
